cq_b5a51289af3f3b3b.luna_worked_solution: In a standard new presentation, the default layout for an added slide is typically Title and Content. The exact layout can depend on the presentation's theme or slide master.
cq_b5a51289af3f3b3b.source_review_reason: The first slide commonly uses Title Slide, subsequent default insertion often Title and Content or inherits layout. Template and current slide context are missing.

cq_7ac01acdcbd0dc7d.question: In Slide Sorter View, what can you do with the slides?
options: Edit the content of the slides
Rearrange the order of the slides
View the presentation in full-screen mode
cq_7ac01acdcbd0dc7d.luna_proposed_option: Rearrange the order of the slides
cq_7ac01acdcbd0dc7d.luna_worked_solution: Slide Sorter View is used to view slide thumbnails and change their sequence by rearranging them.
cq_7ac01acdcbd0dc7d.source_review_reason: Slide Sorter supports rearranging and applying transitions in supported PowerPoint versions, so two listed choices are valid. “Only” content-editing/full-screen are not equivalent, but the stem does not select one valid feature.

cq_68bfe826365b7495.question: Which option should you use to add sound effects to an animation on a slide?
options: Click the "Animations" tab and select "Add Sound"
Right-click the animation and select "Add Sound"
Click the "Insert" tab, then "Audio" and select "Sound"
cq_68bfe826365b7495.luna_worked_solution: In PowerPoint, animation sounds are typically set through the animation's Effect Options (or equivalent effect settings), where a Sound setting is available. None of the listed choices accurately describes that procedure.
cq_68bfe826365b7495.luna_issue: No listed choice uniquely gives the standard procedure: the Animations tab does not generally provide a direct “Add Sound” command, and the animation context menu typically offers Effect Options rather than “Add Sound.” Inserting audio adds an audio object, not a sound effect to an animation.
cq_68bfe826365b7495.source_review_reason: The actual animation-sound workflow uses Effect Options in the Animation Pane/effect dialog; none of the stated menu commands reliably identifies that operation. Insert→Audio adds a separate audio object, not the requested effect sound.

cq_65600c548c0dba21.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of icon on the Windows desktop?
cq_65600c548c0dba21.luna_worked_solution: Shortcut, program, and folder icons are commonly identified as types of Windows desktop icons. “Camera icon” is not one of those general types.
cq_65600c548c0dba21.source_review_reason: A desktop can have a camera application/device shortcut as well as program,folder and shortcut icons. “Camera icon” is not universally excluded without a defined taxonomy.

cq_2d6d30a37f5bfae2.question: IMAP is used for:
options: reading e-mails directly from the server without downloading
cq_2d6d30a37f5bfae2.luna_proposed_option: reading e-mails directly from the server without downloading
cq_2d6d30a37f5bfae2.luna_worked_solution: IMAP lets an email client access and manage messages that remain on the mail server, unlike the traditional POP3 workflow of downloading messages to the client.
cq_2d6d30a37f5bfae2.source_review_reason: IMAP supports server-side mailbox access and selective fetching, but displaying an email still transfers content to the client. “Without downloading” is literally inaccurate; revise to “without requiring the entire mailbox to be downloaded” before certifying the intended choice.
